title: Edit responsiveness
objective: Stop an ordinary edit of a 16 to 60 MP photograph with Detail, Presence and masks from paying seconds, or minutes, for work that buys the person little: the estimate store, mid-drag whole-frame settles, the exact point path through nested spatial segments, GPU previews below 100%, the windowed path behind Detail and Dehaze, colour drags under Dehaze at 100%, and Compare and history re-renders, measured once at the end.
context_summary: On 2026-10-04 a 16 MP RAW edit froze the editor for about four minutes: the status-bar hover readout asked render.sample on every move, the exact point path walked the stage serially through three nested spatial segments, and iced 0.14 ran every owner task on the update loop. The readout is removed, owner tasks run on the runtime's blocking pool and every launch logs. A read-only audit the same day ranked what an ordinary edit still pays for little; docs/design/edit-responsiveness.md records each cost, its evidence and a default the plan runs on, each a proposal until the owner records it (docs/decisions.md, Open product questions). Settled pixels, reports and exports keep their bytes; approximations are motion-only and labelled; every figure is an estimate until TASK-008.

tasks.description: Make the estimate store least-recently-used and large enough to hold a heavy stack's estimates across the proxy, exact and point paths.
extra_context: crates/luxforge-core/src/render/context.rs `EstimateStore`: a VecDeque of ESTIMATE_STORE_ENTRIES (8) entries; `cached` never reorders and `remember` pops the front, so the oldest entry goes whether or not it was just read. A key is (source fingerprint, prefix hash, stage width and height, estimate name); each value is at most MAX_GLOBAL_BYTES (4096), so 256 entries hold at most 1 MiB.

A stack with global Dehaze and three masked Dehaze layers has four estimating units; one job's proxy and exact phases insert eight keys, and every tick or commit with a changed prefix inserts up to four more, so the committed stack's exact-stage lights are gone within about two renders. The consequences are cold serial reductions in point queries and the `region-estimate` and `window-estimate` GPU fallbacks (docs/design/gpu-preview.md, 'after the eight-entry store let it go').

Rule 14: keyed, budgeted, evicting, disposable; the limit is listed in docs/design/architecture.md under Limits. Keep the entry bound a named constant in luxforge_core::modules beside MAX_GLOBAL_BYTES.

tasks.description: Supersede a mid-drag whole-frame settle when the drag goes on, instead of letting it run on the pool under the GPU ticks that follow.
extra_context: crates/luxforge-app/src/app/preview.rs: QUIET_INTERVAL is 120 ms and `quiet_refine` requests PreviewIntent::Settle; crates/luxforge-core/src/preview/worker.rs runs the exact phase, the reduction and Detail's settled display for it. A GPU tick (crates/luxforge-app/src/app/gesture.rs, the gpu_preview_tick path) sends no preview job, so nothing raises the running settle's superseded token; only a CPU tick or a commit replaces it.

Estimated from measured parts for Detail, all three Presence fields and three masked layers: about 1.0 s at 24 MP and 3.1 s at 60 MP of pool work per pause, while the person keeps dragging on the GPU. With exports holding the pool a 24 MP GPU drag reached p95 46 ms against 8.8 to 9.5 ms (docs/specs/performance.md, GPU previews qualified on the M4).

Default: a GPU tick for a newer draft revision supersedes a settle started for an older one and re-arms the quiet timer; the settle after release and the exact settle a commit requests are unchanged. Alternative to record if chosen instead: a longer quiet interval for the whole-frame phase at Fit, keeping 120 ms for 100% region refinement.

tasks.description: Cheapen the exact point path through nested spatial segments: copy held tiles once, evaluate on the pool, and keep the sampled byte the rendered byte.
extra_context: crates/luxforge-core/src/render/spatial.rs `PointTiles::pixel` takes the mutex, scans the held tiles and rotates them per pixel; it is reached per pixel when a later segment's tile input is pulled through an earlier spatial segment (crates/luxforge-core/src/render/pipeline.rs `fill_pulled`, `region_pulled`, `spatial_pixel`), everything runs serially (Parallelism::Serial), and on an estimate miss `build_reduction_by_tiles` walks the whole stage through the earlier tiles.

Measured: 27 to 36 ms through Detail alone, 140 to 227 ms through Clarity and Dehaze behind Basic, 108 to 421 ms for a cold single-segment reduction (docs/specs/performance.md, Point samples through a spatial layer). Three or more segments are unmeasured; 125 to 231 s were observed with a cold miss on a 16 MP RAW with Detail, Presence with Dehaze and masked Presence.

Remaining callers: `render.sample` from any API client; `query.neutral-sample` (25 points before Basic, so through Detail only); `mask.sample-input` and the colour-limited brush seed, whose prefix is the mask's first bound layer's input, three to four segments behind Detail and Presence (crates/luxforge-core/src/editor/pixels.rs, crates/luxforge-core/src/mask/commands/plan.rs). The desktop's remaining samplers run off the update loop, so this is the point worker's time, not the window's.

Default: (a) when a later tile's input region lies within held earlier tiles, copy the overlap from each held tile into the input planes once, falling back to the per-pixel path only for a tile not held; (b) a point query's tile fills and its estimate reduction run on the shared pool under the query's cancel, below the parallel thresholds serially as now (rule 9); (c) exactness: the sampled byte equals the byte an exact render writes, proven through three nested segments in both pixel domains. Alternative recorded in the design: refuse a cold miss with `preparation-required`. The declared exception to rule 4 and its known-costs row are updated with what the change measures.

tasks.description: Draw a drag on the GPU at percentage zooms below 100%, planned at the displayed-size proxy exactly as Fit is.
extra_context: docs/design/gpu-preview.md: below 100% a percentage view plans no GPU preview and the status bar names `not-fit` (crates/luxforge-app/src/app/preview.rs, the percentage branch of the GPU plan request). The CPU path then renders the displayed-size proxy of the whole stage, up to 8 MP, on every tick, roughly 80 to 300 ms at 33% of 60 MP with Detail, Presence and masks (estimate from the Fit figures with the preview off: 41.5/47.2 ms for Texture over Presence on the X100VI, 145/157 ms painting over three masked Presence layers).

The Fit path already plans the GPU preview at the display-bounded proxy and holds the boundary from the same proxy phase; a percentage below 100% differs only in the proxy's size and the view's placement. Budgets, limits, the error limit and the fallback reasons stay as they are; `not-fit` goes.

tasks.description: Accept the windowed and region paths behind Detail and Dehaze when the estimate store holds the exact estimate.
extra_context: crates/luxforge-core/src/render/compiled.rs returns RegionFallback::EstimateAfterSpatial whenever an estimating operation follows a tiled segment, and crates/luxforge-core/src/render/window.rs declines the window; crates/luxforge-core/src/render/entry.rs then plans the whole stage. With Detail before Dehaze, or masked Dehaze after global Presence: 100% motion renders a whole-output proxy fitted to the region, refinement the whole exact frame, and a crop at Fit the whole proxy stage, which grows with the inverse of the crop area; past 256 MiB the GPU boundary is refused (`budget-exceeded`) and past 128 MiB the restoration prefix is not cached (`TooLarge`), so Detail reruns every tick.

docs/design/detail.md, Expected costs: accepting the cut when the store already holds the exact estimate is provably exact and was left out of that plan. The GPU planner already reads a held estimate for the same purpose (`unheld_estimate`). The refusal stays for a cold store.
Depends on the store being large enough to still hold the exact estimate when the window is planned.

tasks.description: Draw a colour drag under Dehaze at 100% without a whole-stage reduction per tick, using the measured reduced light during motion.
extra_context: crates/luxforge-core/src/render/gpu/preview.rs answers GpuFallback::RegionEstimate for a Basic or mask drag at 100% or above with Dehaze present; the CPU interactive region then needs an exact-stage estimate for the drafted prefix, a new key every tick, and the interactive phase reads only the abandoned token, so superseded ticks still run. Measured: 110 to 420 ms per Dehaze unit per cold reduction and 863.91 ms for the first 60 MP Dehaze region (docs/specs/performance.md).

Measured candidate: the light prepared from the drafted colour run over a held reduction costs 2.8 to 6.7 ms per tick at 24 MP and passes 44 of 49 corpus cells (docs/specs/performance.md, Dehaze behind Detail at 100%). Default: during motion only, draw with that light, labelled approximate as every motion frame is, and settle exact; the five failing cells are recorded with their error. Alternative recorded in the design: hold the light the drag started with.
An approximation during motion is a product choice the owner records; the plan runs on the default and the design's proposals table names it.

tasks.description: Re-adopt the retained frame and report when Compare exits or history returns to the picture it left, instead of rendering it again.
extra_context: crates/luxforge-app/src/app/preview.rs keys retained content by one entry; on Compare exit crates/luxforge-app/src/app/history.rs requests a comparison preview with analysis, the current stack's key differs from the last admitted (the Original), the reuse test fails and the proxy and exact phases run again, although crates/luxforge-app/src/app/compare_after.rs still holds the After raster. A history return to the entry just left does the same. Cost: one exact render per toggle, about 1 to 3 s on a heavy stack, for pixels that do not change.

Default: when the content serial of the picture returning equals a retained raster's, present it and its report without a job; otherwise render as today. Alternative recorded in the design: a second content slot, which needs a named limit under rule 6 (92 to 229 MiB on the supplied files).

tasks.description: Measure the finished plan on a quiet M4 and record what changed, including the owner-task hop and the 16 MP stack that froze the editor.
extra_context: Rule 13: release build, quiet host, 30 samples where a distribution is claimed, load recorded around every run; before and after back to back and reversed where a before exists.

Measure: a RAW white-balance release and a slider release's committed frame against the 2026-09 figures (28 against 20 ms p50 for the hop; 539 to 1639 ms release to committed frame on the Z6 and X100VI, now a hop rather than a frozen window); the 16 MP Air 2S stack from the design (lens profile, quarter turn, crop, Basic, curve, mixer, Presence with Dehaze, three masks with Basic and Presence, Sharpening) at 33%: tick, settle after a commit, a mid-drag pause, Compare toggle; a cropped Detail and Dehaze stack at Fit before and after the window cut; a three-segment point sample through the API warm and cold; a Basic drag under Dehaze at 100%.

Record in docs/specs/performance.md with scope and load, update the known-costs rows in docs/engineering/performance-rules.md, the roadmap's GPU previews and edit responsiveness entries and feature status; delete this plan when its outcome is recorded.
